historicalNarration: How can trying to keep your balance make a bridge sway more? On opening day, London’s Millennium Bridge moved sideways. When a walkway shifts, people adjust where they step to stay upright. In a crowd, those sideways forces can feed energy back into the bridge. Instead of dying away, the sway can grow. That can begin without everyone matching footsteps. Later coordination may change the motion; its exact role that day remains uncertain. Engineers added dampers to take energy out of the movement, suppressing the sway.
